newsitem.title: USA: Aviator heads for Africa as part of Earhart flight.
newsitem.headline: Aviator heads for Africa as part of Earhart flight.

text.p: Texas businesswoman and aviator Linda Finch, who is retracing the flight of the legendary Amelia Earhart 60 years ago, set out on Thursday to cross the Atlantic Ocean as part of her round-the-world journey, her spokeswoman said.

Finch, aboard a 1935 Lockheed Electra 10E, the same model used by Earhart in 1937, took off at 3:20 EDT (19:20 GMT) from Natal, Brazil, and would fly overnight to Dakar, Senegal, spokeswoman Beth Fisher said.
The flight was expected to take from 13 to 14 hours in her two-engine plane, which has a maximum speed of about 200 mph (320 kph).
Fisher said the Atlantic crossing would be the most difficult leg of Finch's journey thus far. "The length of the flight will challenge her."
The crossing was delayed by one day due to strong headwinds in Natal. Finch was expected to land in Dakar on Friday morning. From there, she will continue on to Spain, Tunisia, Greece and Egypt.

Finch, a 46-year-old San Antonio businesswoman, took off from Oakland, California, on March 17 at the start of the 30,000-mile (48,000 km), 2-1/2 month trip that follows a route similar to Earhart's 1937 flight. Many of the flight organisers live in the San Francisco Bay area.
Earhart, the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic, completed 22,000 miles (35,400 km) of her journey and vanished in July 1937 on the leg from New Guinea to Howland Island.
Finch's journey, called "World Flight 1997," will span five continents and include more than 30 stops in 20 countries. She is expected to return to Oakland in late May.
